newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks track Wall Street for modest fall.
newsitem.headline: French stocks track Wall Street for modest fall.

text.p: French stocks finished slightly lower on Monday after mirroring a second day of selling on Wall Street, brokers said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.43 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,566.13. The Dow index, whose 2.27 percent fall on Friday prompted an early selloff to as low as 2,528.30, was also down 0.33 percent when the French market closed.
The bourse drew some support from the dollar's strength. "At these levels, the dollar's positive for the bourse," one broker said.
But investors were cautious ahead of U.S. consumer price data due on Tuesday afternoon, and volume was a modest 4.7 billion francs.
Compagnie de Suez shares rose 1.88 percent to 286.60 francs after the resumption of trade on Monday following the formal announcement of its plan to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
The companies said on Friday that Suez shareholders will be offered one share in Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux for 2.05 Suez shares.
Suez, which had been under pressure from its shareholders to pay a special dividend, said it would triple the payout.

"People are happy with the deal," one trader said. Because of the dividend, buying Suez is a safe way to invest in the deal, he said. The rise also anticipates the parities for the proposed share exchange. Lyonnaise shares closed up 0.19 percent at 541 francs.
